chapterBreakdown.gentle: A strategy can sound exciting until someone asks how it is supposed to work. Bossidy and Charan use Chapter 7 to argue that strategy is not an isolated planning document. It is a process linked to people and operations, and it has to explain the hows instead of only naming the destination. The chapter then shows what a real strategic plan has to answer. It has to face the environment, customers, markets, competition, capability, milestones, and the balance between short-term and long-term demands. It also has to stay honest about critical issues and about how the business will make money on a sustainable basis. Without those answers, strategy becomes ambition with polished language.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Strategy becomes an execution process rather than a vision statement here. Bossidy and Charan keep pushing on the hows because direction without mechanism is too weak to carry a business. The plan has to answer practical questions about environment, customers, competition, execution capability, milestones, and time balance. It also has to face critical issues and sustainable economics. The chapter's edge is simple: a strategy is only serious when it can be carried by real people through real operations.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: A strategy is cheap until it can answer how it will win. Bossidy and Charan make Chapter 7 press strategy through customers, competition, capability, milestones, and sustainable economics instead of letting it hide inside ambition talk. Link the plan to people and operations or stop calling it executable. If the hows are vague, the strategy is still dressed up hope.

chapterBreakdown.gentle: A strategy can sound impressive while still being too thin to carry the business. Bossidy and Charan pressure that weakness in Chapter 7 by tying strategy directly to people and operations. The chapter does not let strategy live as a polished planning document. It asks whether the plan can explain how the business will move, compete, and execute in the real world. That is why the importance of the hows comes first. A destination without a route is not yet a strategy in this frame. The chapter then moves into the building blocks of a strategy, the making of the strategic plan, and the question of who builds it. Those points matter because ownership affects realism. If the people who must carry the plan are too far from shaping it, then the strategy can become cleaner than the business itself. The chapter then turns outward through the environment, existing customers and markets, competition, and the best path to profitable growth. It turns inward through execution capability, milestones, and the balance between short term and long term. The chapter closes by forcing the plan to face critical issues and sustainable profit logic. A strategy stays real only when it can answer those questions without hiding inside ambition language.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Strategy becomes an execution process here, not a statement of preference. Bossidy and Charan insist that the plan has to stay linked to people and operations, which makes the hows unavoidable. The chapter then builds strategy through practical questions: what the environment is doing, what customers and markets require, who the competition is, how the business will grow profitably, whether the organization can execute, what milestones will prove motion, how short-term and long-term balance will be handled, what critical issues threaten the plan, and whether the economics are sustainable. These are not add-ons. They are tests that distinguish a strategic plan from attractive direction language. The chapter also cares about who builds the plan because disconnected ownership weakens realism. A strategy that sounds bold but has no carrying capacity, no milestone logic, and no durable economic case is still too soft to trust.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: A strategy either answers the hard questions or hides behind polished ambition. Bossidy and Charan force Chapter 7 onto that line by linking strategy to people and operations and by insisting on the hows. Once that demand lands, the rest of the chapter becomes a realism gauntlet: environment, customers, competition, profitable growth, execution capability, milestones, time balance, critical issues, and sustainable economics. Skip those questions and the plan may still sound sharp while staying empty. The chapter also refuses the fantasy that a plan can be built far from the people who will carry it. Ownership matters because abstract authorship breeds abstract strategy. The chapter's harder pressure is clear: a business cannot call its direction strategic if it has not forced that direction through the field, the organization, and the economics that decide whether it can endure.

chapterBreakdown.gentle: Strategy often becomes most dangerous when it sounds most elevated, because elevation can hide missing mechanism. Bossidy and Charan resist that drift in Chapter 7 by linking strategy directly to people and operations and by insisting on the importance of the hows. In their frame, strategy is not validated by breadth of vision or by confidence of tone. It is validated by whether the business can explain how it will move through the environment, serve existing customers and markets, grow profitably, face competition, execute with available or buildable capability, hit meaningful milestones, balance short-term and long-term demands, confront critical issues, and make money on a sustainable basis. That turns strategy into a discipline of realism rather than a language of aspiration. The chapter also cares about who builds the plan because authorship affects whether the strategy can remain honest about what the business can carry. A plan built too far from the people who must execute it can become structurally flattering. The harder edge of the chapter is that strategy theater does not always look unserious. It can look organized, ambitious, and intelligent while still refusing to answer the questions that expose whether the route, the organization, and the economics can hold together.
chapterBreakdown.direct: Strategy becomes a process of practical exposure here. Bossidy and Charan force the strategy process to answer to people and operations first, which means the plan cannot hide in a detached document. The importance of the hows becomes decisive because the business must explain not only what it wants but how it expects to win, grow, and execute. From there the chapter builds a strategic-plan gauntlet: external environment, customers and markets, competition, profitable growth path, execution capability, milestones, short-term and long-term balance, critical issues, and sustainable profit logic. None of those questions are ornamental. They are the means by which strategy is stripped of self-flattering vagueness. The chapter's concern with who builds the plan deepens the same point. Ownership matters because realism weakens when strategy is authored in abstraction and carried elsewhere. The harder lesson is that strategy is not automatically serious because it is comprehensive. It becomes serious only when it can survive these field, capability, sequencing, and economics tests without depending on unearned confidence.
chapterBreakdown.competitive: A strategy can wear the costume of rigor while still dodging the questions that decide whether it can live. Bossidy and Charan make Chapter 7 tear off that costume. Link the plan to people and operations or admit it is floating. Force it to explain the hows or admit it is still selling mood. Then drive it through the field: environment, customers, competition, and profitable growth. Drive it through the organization: capability, milestones, and ownership. Drive it through time and economics: short-term pressure, long-term balance, critical issues, and sustainable profit. What survives that pressure is strategy. What does not survive it was ambition theater all along. The chapter's edge is not anti-vision. It is anti-delusion. It refuses to let direction language outrun the carrying capacity, competitive reality, and durable logic required to make the direction worth trusting.
